summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update11.json → valid=true; the first patch attempt failed on malformed hunk headers and was re-issued cleanly). Third adversarial pass on the election-threshold finding, aimed at the retained material best placed to falsify it: the fuzzy framework's appendEntriesVerifier states and enforces 'only one node sends AppendEntries for any given term' — it records the first claimant per term and errors when another node sends for that term, or when the request's declared leader does not match the sender (fuzzy/verifier.go:14-80) — and it is installed in the membership scenarios, which remove a live leader from a five-node cluster and partition a node away before removing it, with writes running before and after and logs/FSMs verified (fuzzy/membership_test.go:79-118). Because any node that takes leadership immediately dispatches a no-op AppendEntries, this invariant is sensitive to the split-vote consequence. Recorded as one Fact plus a second successor interpretation for the same question: the mechanism claims (threshold captured once per candidacy, win test against that captured value, and the two receive paths that can change configurations.latest mid-candidacy) are unchanged, the previously added grant gate is unchanged, and the stronger consequence is kept conditional on gate-open plus a same-term configuration-growing message reaching the candidacy — explicitly not claimed as a demonstrated reachable split-brain. Counterevidence is preserved and extended: the fuzzy scenarios are randomized and time-bounded so a passing suite narrows practical severity without proving the mechanism absent; the verifier only observes AppendEntries senders; and no retained scenario combines a TimeoutNow-induced candidacy with a same-term rival and a configuration-growing entry, so that conjunction is exercised neither positively nor negatively. Both earlier interpretations remain available, and no execution was performed (fuzzy framework read, not run).
